title: Bond enthalpies; Sigma/pi, hybridization and resonance; formal charge
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN03#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t4 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD07#N.5, EN03#N.5b, BD07#N.7, EN03#N.10b, BD07#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Exothermic
items.clue: Describes the forming of a bond: energy is released.

items.label: Free rotation
items.clue: Groups can turn about a single C–C link, but not about C=C.

items.label: Trigonal planar
items.clue: Arrangement around each C of C=C: three bonding regions at about 120°.

items.label: Pi bond
items.clue: Sideways overlap of two p orbitals, with electron density above and below the axis.

questions.stem: A student hypothesizes that a pi bond between two carbon atoms prevents rotation about the bond that joins them. Which observation does this hypothesis predict?

options.text: ClHC=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClH₂C–CH₂Cl exists as two separable compounds
H₂C=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClC≡CCl exists as two separable compounds

questions.explanation: With no rotation, the two Cl atoms are fixed on the same side or opposite sides of C=C: two isomers. ClH₂C–CH₂Cl has no π bond, so it rotates and is one compound.

questions.stem: Hydrogen and fluorine react exothermically: H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2 HF(g). The reaction can be thought of as taking place in two stages: the bonds in the reactant molecules break, and then the bonds in the product molecules form. Which statement correctly describes the potential energy of the system during these stages?

options.text: It falls as the H–H and F–F bonds break and rises as the H–F bonds form
It rises as the H–H and F–F bonds break and rises as the H–F bonds form
It rises as the H–H and F–F bonds break and falls as the H–F bonds form
It falls as the H–H and F–F bonds break and falls as the H–F bonds form

questions.explanation: Separating atoms raises the potential energy; forming H–F bonds lowers it, by more than it rose, because the reaction is exothermic.

questions.stem: In which molecule is the central atom sp² hybridized?

options.text: H₂O
SO₂
NH₃
CO₂

questions.explanation: S has two bonding domains and one lone pair: three domains, so sp², with ideal angles of 120°.

questions.stem: For the reaction H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2 HCl(g), ΔH° = −184.6 kJ/mol_rxn. The bond enthalpy of the H–H bond is 436 kJ/mol, and the bond enthalpy of the Cl–Cl bond is 243 kJ/mol. Based on these data, what is the bond enthalpy of the H–Cl bond?

options.text: 247 kJ/mol
864 kJ/mol
524 kJ/mol
432 kJ/mol

questions.stem: Average bond enthalpies: C–C 347 kJ/mol · C=C 612 kJ/mol · C≡C 838 kJ/mol. A C≡C bond is only about 2.4 times as strong as a C–C bond, not 3 times. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its three shared pairs repel one another, so C≡C is longer than C–C.
All three of its bonds are σ bonds, but they are weaker because they share space.
Two of its three bonds come from sideways overlap of p orbitals, which is less effective.
Its π electrons lie on the axis between the nuclei, where σ electrons repel them.

questions.explanation: C≡C is one σ and two π. Each π adds less than a σ: 612 − 347 = 265, then 838 − 612 = 226. So the total is well below 3 × 347 = 1041.
